observations.detail: 'Save changes' and 'Unsaved changes' sit below the fold of the upper pane (y≈655, behind the tab bar at y≈512), so the user must scroll the upper pane to reach them. A click at the button's semantic position lands on the dispute list below instead. This isn't caused by the theme change: an earlier semantics dump showed the same position. The button itself is painted at 153x38 and saves once scrolled into view.

observations.area: Notifications bell badge (still present after the re-run)
observations.detail: With unread notifications, the '99+' badge (19x16 at 1165,23; on phone 303,23) covers the bell's centre and swallows taps. A click on the badge does nothing, with or without unsaved edits; a click on the lower-left of the bell works (prompts when dirty, else opens #/notifications). Likely cause: the Positioned badge is stacked over the IconButton in frontend/lib/shared/widgets/app_shell.dart (_NotificationsBell Stack, ~lines 189-198 in the current file) and wins the hit test. An IgnorePointer around the badge would let taps through.

observations.area: Sales POC picker (D-18, not part of this fix set)
observations.detail: On the invoice form, typing the full username 'vu-sales-mu2ylll4f82e' in 'Choose Sales POC' left the list unfiltered (AURRC…, AURSB…). Adding and deleting a space made it filter to the one user. So D-18 is still present in PocPicker; the new SearchPickerField does not have this lag.

After B was cancelled, the promise card still showed 'INV-20260915-0432 • ₹100.00 left' for the cancelled invoice, while the edit dialog says 'no longer owed'. The chip uses the balance with no status check: frontend/lib/features/promises/promises_tab.dart:186.
At 400x820 the invoice number still breaks mid-token ('INV-20 / 26091 / 5-0428').

POST /api/disputes as admin returns 403 'You do not have permission for this action', so the test disputes (#147-#150) were opened with customer logins. Only one open dispute per invoice is allowed (400 'An open dispute already exists for this invoice'). Admin detail screens do show a 'Raise dispute' button; its behaviour for admin was not exercised here.

Switching to a non-default tab changes the URL (?tab=history) and adds one browser history entry (d11r: 4 -> 5). So after a tab switch, the first browser Back returns to the previous tab of the same record (no prompt, by design) rather than asking to leave. Not a defect by itself; noted because it affects 'the next Back prompts' when tabs were used.
